title: Replace a refrigerator start relay
author: Marco R.
parts: start relay matching the fridge model

steps.instruction: Pull the fridge away from the wall and unplug it from the outlet.
steps.expected_state: The power cord's plug is visibly out of the wall outlet, with both the plug and the empty outlet in the same frame.
steps.verify_hints: Reject if the cord is still in the outlet or if the plug is not in frame. A switched-off thermostat does not count.
common_mistakes: Turning the thermostat off instead of unplugging
Only showing the plug without the outlet
steps.gate_requirement: Fridge disconnected from mains power, plug visibly out of the outlet.

steps.instruction: Remove the rear access panel at the bottom back of the fridge. It is usually held by four screws.
steps.expected_state: The rear access panel is off and the compressor (a black dome-shaped unit) is exposed.
steps.verify_hints: Compressor must be visible. Screws out of frame is fine.
common_mistakes: Removing the wrong panel (the condenser fan cover)

steps.instruction: Unclip the plastic relay cover on the side of the compressor. There is a tab at the bottom.
steps.expected_state: The relay cover is off and the start relay (a black rectangular box plugged onto the compressor) is exposed with its wires still attached.
steps.verify_hints: The relay should still be attached in this step. If it is already off, that is step 4 and still passes here.
common_mistakes: Prying the cover from the top and cracking it

steps.instruction: Pull the old start relay straight off the compressor pins. Grip the body, not the wires. Wiggle gently, do not twist.
steps.expected_state: The relay is detached from the compressor and three bare metal pins are visible on the compressor body.
steps.verify_hints: All three pins must be visible. If a hand or the relay hides any pin, ask for a photo from below at about 20 cm.

steps.instruction: Push the new relay onto the three pins with its notch facing the overload protector, until it seats with a click.
steps.expected_state: The new relay is seated flush on the compressor pins with the notch on the relay facing the overload protector (the small block next to it).
steps.verify_hints: Orientation is the whole test. Notch away from the overload protector is a fail. If the notch is hidden, ask for a photo straight on from the side.

steps.instruction: Reconnect the wire harness to the relay and snap the relay cover back on.
steps.expected_state: The relay cover is back in place with the wire harness entering it; no loose connectors visible.
steps.verify_hints: Any dangling connector is a fail.
common_mistakes: Pinching a wire under the cover

steps.instruction: Refit the rear access panel, plug the fridge back in, and listen for the compressor to start within about a minute.
steps.expected_state: The rear panel is back on and the plug is in the outlet. A clip with audible compressor hum is ideal.
steps.verify_hints: Pass on panel refitted and plug in. If a clip is sent, listen for a steady hum rather than a repeated click, which means the relay is still wrong.
common_mistakes: Plugging in before the panel is on
